manual_source.scope: Manual layouts and code tables compared against original CSV values; no raw records overwritten

errata.conflict: Semiconductor diagram S versus prose C / Fixed Capacitor
errata.resolution: Use diagram S; subtype SS/ST/SF and remaining layout are CSV-supported extensions, not definitions from this page

errata.conflict: Variable resistor diagram 17 versus prose 18; switch entries are mixed with thermistors
errata.resolution: Use 17 for 75/76 thermistors, supported by CSV; explicitly support observed 1701 legacy switch but route new switches to 18
Use diagram 19, supported by CSV connector rows

decisions: Thermistors 1775/1776 have 7-character part identifier, Packing at position 12, manufacturer/version at position 13
Separate six logical slot outputs from the actual category-specific order and widths
Reject prefix-plus-length-only matches when code table values are invalid
Keep out-of-manual customer and legacy codes unchanged as registered candidates; do not infer their segment semantics
Train detailed heads only from rule-validated reversible labels; fit selection on training folds only
Retain source and schema validation information for every output
Do not generate or reserve new serial identifiers from nearest neighbors
Fuse: 25 + 2-character subtype + 8-character series/current + 1-character version; Packing is not a fuse slot
Varistor: PDF p28 code tables plus CSV-confirmed physical positions. Disk=2590 + shape3 + identifier4 + pack1 + vendor1; Chip=2591 + shape2 + identifier5 + pack1 + vendor1

The PDF varistor paragraph says six identifier characters, inconsistent with its 13-position layout and CSV. The decoded widths are explicitly marked manual_and_csv, without changing any original code
